newsitem.title: ITALY: Dini's Italian Renewal boosts parliament strength.
newsitem.headline: Dini's Italian Renewal boosts parliament strength.

text.p: A parliamentarian from Italy's opposition centre-right bloc said on Monday that he had switched ranks to Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's centrist Italian Renewal party.
Stefano Bastianoni from the CCD-CDU party group said in a statement that he believed Italian Renewal was the right place to work for a strong centrist force in national politics.

Italian Renewal had announced that another opposition deputy, Nicola Miraglia Del Giudice, had also joined its ranks but the defection was denied by Del Giudice's hard-right National Alliance (AN) party.
Political sources said Del Giudice had been talked out of changing parties by AN leader Gianfranco Fini.
Bastianoni's switch will increase the centre-left government's majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).

It also takes Italian Renewal's strength in the lower house to the 20 deputies it needs to form its own parliamentary group with the right to name a representative to a new commission on constitutional reform formed by the two houses of parliament.
Dini created Italian Renewal before the April general election last year while serving as stop-gap prime minister.
It had 26 deputies after the election but a split cut its strength to 14. The other 12 remain loyal to the government.
AN and CCD-CDU are part of media magnate Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance bloc.
Two members of Berlusconi's Forza Italia switched to Italian Renewal earlier this month. Three pro-government deputies also joined the party from other forces, bringing the total to 19.
The centre ground of Italian politics has been fragmented and in flux since the demise of the long dominant Christian Democrat party in the country's corruption scandals.
Dini is pushing for a consolidation of the centre across the government-opposition divide.
